rules.name: SSH brute force
rules.description: Many failed SSH logins from one address in a short time.

rules.name: Successful login after brute force
rules.description: An address that had been failing logins repeatedly then got in. Either the guessing worked or someone finally remembered their password; both are worth a look.

rules.name: Password spraying
rules.description: One address trying many different usernames, the pattern of testing one common password everywhere.

rules.name: Account used from many addresses
rules.description: One account logging in successfully from several different addresses within an hour.

rules.name: Direct root login over SSH
rules.description: Root logged in directly over SSH instead of a named user escalating with sudo.

rules.name: Sensitive command run with sudo
rules.description: sudo used on credential files, account management, setuid bits or reverse shells.

rules.name: Port scan
rules.description: One address hitting many different blocked ports in a short time.

rules.name: SQL injection attempt
rules.description: Request path or query string contains SQL injection syntax.

rules.name: Path traversal or sensitive file probe
rules.description: Request tries to climb out of the web root or fetch files that should never be served.

rules.name: Known scanning tool
rules.description: The client identifies itself as an attack or scanning tool.

rules.name: Web content discovery
rules.description: A burst of not-found and forbidden responses to one address, typical of directory brute forcing.
